summary: devfs_hosttest.c and procfs_hosttest.c, the opens, reads and writes of /dev and /proc files, with faults in private copies of rach2/sys/fs/devfs.c and procfs.c

argv:
set -eu
t=${WORK}/tree
sh tests/proofs/tree.sh "$t" ${SRC} rach2/sys tests/host
cd "$t"
s=rach2/sys
for test in devfs procfs; do
    deps=$(grep -oE 'host-deps:[^*]*' tests/host/${test}_hosttest.c | sed 's/host-deps://' | tr '\n' ' ')
    ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 -DRACH2_HOSTTEST -g -O1 -ffreestanding -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wno-unused-function -Wno-pointer-to-int-cast -Wno-int-to-pointer-cast -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -I $s -I $s/arch/x86 -I $s/arch/i686 -I $s/lib -I $s/proc tests/host/${test}_hosttest.c $deps -o ${WORK}/${test}_hosttest
done

export UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=0:exitcode=1
status=0
${WORK}/devfs_hosttest || status=$?
${WORK}/procfs_hosttest || { s=$?; [ "$status" -ne 0 ] || status=$s; }
exit "$status"

faults.name: ptmx
faults.summary: a ptmx open dispatched before the checks of its flags

lines: devfs-hosttest: fail: ptmx exclusive create returns EEXIST before dispatch

faults.name: screenlog-unheld
faults.summary: the screen log dropped from the devices whose transfers move the offset

edits.find: return e && e->type == FD_TYPE_DEVICE && e->dev && e->dev->ops == &screenlog_ops;

lines: devfs-hosttest: fail: a read of /dev/screenlog holds its description, as it moves the offset

faults.name: terminator
faults.summary: a text's terminator written with no buffer

lines: runtime error: store to null pointer

faults.name: mem-hold
faults.summary: a /proc/PID/mem open that takes a user of the address space, not a hold

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: an open of /proc/PID/mem holds the record and is no user of it

faults.name: mem-live
faults.summary: a /proc/PID/mem read that takes a user when no user remains

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: a read once the process has ended returns 0 and reaches no memory

faults.name: exe-present
faults.summary: an exe link without the program's present path

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: the link reads a renamed program's present path

faults.name: exe-deleted
faults.summary: an exe link without its deleted mark

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: a program whose name is gone reads as its exec's path, deleted

faults.name: unheld-space
faults.summary: a read of a process's arguments that holds no reference to the address space

faults.name: record-after-sleep
faults.summary: a read of a process's arguments that reads the process's record after the first read, which may sleep

faults.name: hold-not-user
faults.summary: a read of a process's arguments that takes a hold, not a user

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: a read of the arguments reaches pages a user keeps

faults.name: oom-range
faults.summary: an oom_score_adj write that takes a value out of range

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: a value past -1000 to 1000 is EINVAL and changes nothing

faults.name: oom-floor
faults.summary: an oom_score_adj write that lowers the value below the floor without privilege

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: and may not lower it below the floor

faults.name: oom-floor-kept
faults.summary: an oom_score_adj write that leaves the floor where a privileged write found it

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: a privileged write sets the floor

faults.name: oom-open-emfile
faults.summary: an open of oom_score_adj that answers EMFILE where the heap has no room

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: an open of oom_score_adj the heap has no room for is ENOMEM

faults.name: oom-nbsp
faults.summary: a parse of oom_score_adj that takes byte 0xA0 for no space

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: the byte 0xa0 at either end is a space, as Linux's isspace has it

faults.name: oom-range-first
faults.summary: a parse of oom_score_adj that answers ERANGE for text that is no integer

lines: procfs-hosttest: fail: text that is no integer is EINVAL however many digits it begins with
